Done.

About the ghosts in Photos.app: the bytes are off your phone, but Photos.app still has database entries that point to the now-missing files. They show up as photos with a small ! badge and "unable to load higher quality version".

To clean them up: open Photos > Library > All Photos on your iPhone > tap any ghost > Select > Select All > Trash > then open Albums > Recently Deleted > Select > Delete All. Two steps. Automation tracked at issue #1.

FYI: iPhone storage takes a few minutes to fully reflect freed bytes after a large dump — that's iOS lazily reindexing.

Are you sure?

Password-protect this backup

DumpSock will encrypt the .zip with AES-256-GCM. The key is derived from your password via PBKDF2-SHA256 (200,000 iterations).

If you lose this password the backup is unreadable. No reset, no recovery — that's the point.

Wring it dry?

After every file is safely written to disk, DumpSock will remove it from /var/mobile/Media/DCIM/ on your iPhone over USB. Storage is freed immediately.

Only the files actually written to your chosen output folder will be removed. Files that fail to transfer, or whose size doesn't verify, are never deleted.

Photos.app will show ghost entries for the removed files. To clean those up: select them in Photos.app and delete them, then empty Recently Deleted. We're automating that one-Touch-ID flow next (see issue #1).
